intuition.summary: Cochains as measurements: a k-cochain assigns a number to each k-simplex; cocycles are locally consistent data, coboundaries are data that are trivially consistent, and cohomology measures the obstruction to globalising. Illustrated by the Mobius band twist detected by H^1 of the circle.

Degree-one cocycles on a surface can be represented by counting signed crossings with a transverse curve; a cup product of two such classes is nonzero exactly when the corresponding loops are forced to intersect. In the nonorientable case a curve cannot be pushed off itself, explaining why its square is nonzero mod 2.
intuition.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.2 Cup Product (pp. 206-229)

intuition.summary: Under Poincare duality, cup product corresponds to transverse intersection of dual submanifolds (codimensions add); on a lattice, a p-cochain is pictured as a (d-p)-dimensional surface on the dual cellulation.
intuition.source: Chen, Tata, Higher cup products on hypercubic lattices, arXiv:2106.05274, Sec. II

intuition.summary: Making intersection = cup product precise at the cochain level: intersection is commutative but only partially defined, the cubical cup product is total but commutative only up to homotopy; flowing one submanifold forward and the other backward along a canonical vector field makes the two agree.
intuition.source: Friedman, Medina-Mardones, Sinha, Flowing from intersection product to cup product, arXiv:2106.05986, Sec. 1

intuition.summary: Integral degree-one classes are circle-valued functions: a 1-cocycle with integer values integrates to a map to S^1 = R/Z; this is the basis of circular coordinates in data analysis.
intuition.source: Scoccola et al., Toroidal coordinates, arXiv:2212.07201, Sec. 2-4, App. A.2

intuition.summary: Cup-length as a count of how many classes can be multiplied nontrivially, a crude measure of the ring that bounds Lusternik-Schnirelmann category and distinguishes spaces with equal Betti numbers.
intuition.source: Contessoto, Memoli, Stefanou, Zhou, Persistent cup-length, arXiv:2107.01553, Sec. 3

motivation.summary: History: Poincare (1893-95) stated duality of Betti numbers, first via intersections and then via dual triangulations after Heegaard's criticism; the cohomological restatement with cup and cap products came from Cech and Whitney in the 1930s.

Timeline: Alexander-Lefschetz intersection theory (1920s) as precursor of the cup product; de Rham (1931); Kolmogorov and Alexander introduce cohomology (1935); Cech/Whitney cup and cap products (1936-38); Eilenberg's singular definition (1944); Eilenberg-Steenrod axioms (1945-52); Leray's sheaf cohomology (1946).
Why cohomology beyond homology: contravariance fits pullback of functions, and the cup product makes it a ring, a strictly stronger homotopy invariant (e.g. CP^2 vs S^2 v S^4, torus vs wedge).
Ring structure as a tool for nonexistence results: Hatcher uses cohomology rings of projective spaces to show R^n has a division algebra structure only for n a power of 2, and CP^2 is not S^2 v S^4.
motivation.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.2 Cup Product (pp. 206-229)

motivation.summary: In applied work the motivation is extra discriminating power at low cost: persistent cup-length distinguishes filtrations (T^2 vs S^1 v S^2 v S^1) that barcodes cannot.
motivation.source: Contessoto, Memoli, Stefanou, Zhou, Persistent cup-length, arXiv:2107.01553, Sec. 3

definitions.summary: Singular cochains C^n(X;G)=Hom(C_n(X),G), coboundary dual to boundary, so arrows reverse; relative cochains vanish on chains in A.

Cup product via front and back faces: (phi cup psi)(sigma) = phi(sigma restricted to [v0..vk]) times psi(sigma restricted to [vk..vk+l]); Leibniz formula delta(phi cup psi)= delta phi cup psi + (-1)^k phi cup delta psi; descends to an associative unital ring.
definitions.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.2 Cup Product (pp. 206-229)

definitions.summary: Equivalent definition: cup product = cross product (Kunneth/Alexander-Whitney map) followed by pullback along the diagonal X -> X x X; the Alexander-Whitney map is unique up to chain homotopy by acyclic models, so the cohomology product does not depend on the choice; with the standard choice it is strictly associative.

Categorical definition: precompose the external product of cocycles with the diagonal and apply a coefficient pairing A1 x A2 -> A3; singular case is Moore cochains on the singular simplicial set; cochains form an E-infinity algebra (Berger-Fresse).

Representability: reduced H^n(X;G) is in natural bijection with based homotopy classes [X, K(G,n)], the class corresponding to pulling back the fundamental class; K(Z,1)=S^1, K(Z,2)=CP^infinity, K(Z/2,1)=RP^infinity.

Cap product: sigma cap phi = phi(front k-face) times back l-face; characterised by psi(alpha cap phi) = (phi cup psi)(alpha); boundary formula with sign (-1)^k; naturality f_*(alpha) cap phi = f_*(alpha cap f^* phi).
definitions.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.3, cap product passage

definitions.summary: Homological orientation: local orientation = generator of H_n(M, M-x) (infinite cyclic); orientation double cover; closed connected M orientable iff H_n(M)=Z, an orientation is a choice of generator (fundamental class).

General Poincare duality: for compact K contained in an R-oriented n-manifold M, cap with [M]_K gives Cech H^p(K,L;R) -> H_{n-p}(M-L, M-K;R) isomorphisms; compact M gives H^p(M;R) = H_{n-p}(M;R). Proved by Mayer-Vietoris induction from convex sets in R^n plus a limit argument.
definitions.source: Miller, MIT 18.905 Fall 2016 lecture 37: Poincare duality

definitions.summary: Axiomatic definition: cohomology characterised by Eilenberg-Steenrod axioms; on CW complexes it is unique and computed cellularly; May develops singular and cellular cohomology as instances.
definitions.source: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology (revised), contents

definitions.summary: Cohomology UCT: natural short exact sequence 0 -> Ext(H_{n-1}(X),G) -> H^n(X;G) -> Hom(H_n(X),G) -> 0 over a PID, split but not naturally; over a field cohomology is the dual of homology.
Field case proved directly: Kronecker pairing descends to (co)homology and linear algebra on annihilators gives H^q = dual of H_q with field coefficients, including for pairs.
definitions.source: UC Riverside Math 246A (2022) notes, Unit IV.2 'A weak Universal Coefficient Theorem', pp.115-117

definitions.summary: Poincare duality spaces: finite(ly dominated) complexes with a class [X] such that cap product is an isomorphism for all local systems twisted by an orientation character; several inequivalent historical definitions (Browder, Spivak, Wall).
definitions.source: Klein, Qin, Su, On the various notions of Poincare duality space, arXiv:1901.00145, Sec. 1, 8

viewpoints.summary: Algebraic/combinatorial: explicit cochain formulas on ordered simplicial complexes and cubical complexes, implementable as algorithms.
viewpoints.source: Contessoto, Memoli, Stefanou, Zhou, Persistent cup-length, arXiv:2107.01553, Sec. 3

viewpoints.summary: Geometric: cohomology classes as Poincare duals of submanifolds; cup = intersection; mod 2 intersection on lattices.
viewpoints.source: Chen, Tata, Higher cup products on hypercubic lattices, arXiv:2106.05274, Sec. II

viewpoints.summary: Homotopical: H^n(-;G) represented by K(G,n); cohomology operations = H^n(K(G,m);H); cup product from maps K(A,p) x K(B,q) -> K(A tensor B, p+q).
Higher-structure: cochain cup product is only homotopy commutative; E-infinity algebra structure, Steenrod cup-i products.
Analytic: with real coefficients singular cohomology agrees with de Rham, cup product = wedge of forms; integrality of periods.
Data-analytic: persistent cohomology of Vietoris-Rips filtrations, representative cocycles giving coordinates and cup-length invariants.
viewpoints.source: Scoccola et al., Toroidal coordinates, arXiv:2212.07201, Sec. 2-4, App. A.2

conventions.summary: Coboundary sign: Hatcher and Munkres use delta_n = (partial_{n+1})^*; Bredon uses delta_n = (-1)^{n+1} (partial_{n+1})^*. Cup product then differs by (-1)^{kl} and cap product by (-1)^{k(l-k)} between Hatcher and Bredon; consequent sign changes in Bockstein/duality diagrams and intersection forms.
conventions.source: Conway, Friedl, Herrmann, Linking forms revisited, arXiv:1708.03754, Sec. 2

conventions.summary: Dold's convention agrees with Koszul signs everywhere except the coboundary; Friedman-McClure follow Dold but add a sign (-1)^{in} to Poincare duality so it is a Koszul-compatible chain map of degree dim X; Appendix argues some sign issues are unavoidable.
conventions.source: Friedman, McClure, Intersection homology duality and pairings: singular, PL and sheaf-theoretic, arXiv:1812.10585, Sec. 2 'Signs' and App. B

conventions.summary: Dold-style coboundary with extra minus sign delta alpha(c) = -(-1)^{|alpha|} alpha(partial c), used in intersection-homology notes.
conventions.source: Chriestenson, notes 'intersection, cup and cap products' (intersection homology), WOU-hosted pdf

conventions.summary: Cap product order: Hatcher writes the chain on the left (alpha cap phi) and uses psi(alpha cap phi) = (phi cup psi)(alpha); Wikipedia also writes chain on the left, making homology a right module over cohomology; other books put the cochain first (unverified which).
conventions.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.3, cap product passage

conventions.summary: Integer versions of cup-i products differ in sign conventions from Steenrod's original formulas.
conventions.source: Chen, Tata, Higher cup products on hypercubic lattices, arXiv:2106.05274, Sec. II

conventions.summary: Boundary orientation convention outward-normal-first gives partial[M]=[partial M]; intersection form sign Q(x,y) = -<PD(x),y> appears under Hatcher conventions.
conventions.source: Conway, Friedl, Herrmann, Linking forms revisited, arXiv:1708.03754, Sec. 2

conventions.summary: Front face/back face (Alexander-Whitney) is the standard cup product convention; cubical analog uses the Serre diagonal with shuffle signs; evaluation of tensor products of cochains differs from Dold's Koszul convention.
conventions.source: Friedman, Medina-Mardones, Sinha, Flowing from intersection product to cup product, arXiv:2106.05986, Sec. 1

examples.summary: Orientable genus g surface: classes a_i, b_i with a_i b_i = generator = -b_i a_i, all other products zero (symplectic form); nonorientable surfaces and RP^2 with Z/2: a^2 nonzero.
examples.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.2 Cup Product (pp. 206-229)

examples.summary: Same groups, different rings: torus vs S^1 v S^1 v S^2 (products of degree-one classes vanish in the wedge); CP^2 vs S^2 v S^4.
Projective spaces: H*(RP^n;Z/2)=Z/2[a]/(a^{n+1}), |a|=1; H*(CP^n;Z)=Z[a]/(a^{n+1}), |a|=2; HP^n with |a|=4; infinite versions polynomial; H*(RP^infinity;Z)=Z[a]/(2a), |a|=2.
examples.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.2 Cup Product (pp. 206-229)

examples.summary: Space with a 2-cell attached by degree m: Z/m coefficients see a nonzero square when m even, showing integer coefficients alone can hide ring structure.
examples.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.2 Cup Product (pp. 206-229)

examples.summary: Spheres Z[x]/(x^2), tori exterior algebra, point, contractible spaces; products of spheres via Kunneth.
RP^n with integer coefficients computed from homology via UCT: torsion shifts up one degree.
Lens spaces and linking forms: the torsion linking form via Bockstein and PD; sign subtleties for lens spaces.
examples.source: Conway, Friedl, Herrmann, Linking forms revisited, arXiv:1708.03754, Sec. 2

examples.summary: Flag manifolds and classifying spaces: H*(BU(n))=Z[c_1..c_n], H*(BT^n) polynomial on degree-2 classes, Borel presentation of H*(Fl_n).

computation.summary: Compute cohomology groups from homology via the UCT (Ext term from torsion in degree n-1), or directly from cellular cochains.

Ring structure via Kunneth: H*(X x Y) = H*(X) tensor H*(Y) as rings with sign (a x b)(c x d)=(-1)^{|b||c|} ac x bd when H^k(Y;R) is finitely generated free (CW complexes); relative version for CW pairs.
computation.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.2 Cup Product (pp. 206-229)

computation.summary: Poincare duality forces products: in CP^n, nondegeneracy of the cup pairing in complementary degrees gives a^k generators inductively (Hatcher's proof of Theorem 3.19).
computation.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.2 Cup Product (pp. 206-229)

computation.summary: Naturality/ring homomorphisms: pull back along maps (e.g. to a wedge of tori for surfaces, inclusion of torus in BU(n)) to detect products.
computation.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.2 Cup Product (pp. 206-229)

computation.summary: Explicit cochain-level algorithms for cup products on simplicial complexes, with complexity bounds; restriction to subcomplexes for filtrations.
computation.source: Contessoto, Memoli, Stefanou, Zhou, Persistent cup-length, arXiv:2107.01553, Sec. 3

computation.summary: Multiplicative spectral sequences (Serre) to compute rings of fibrations; differentials as derivations.
Mayer-Vietoris induction (local-to-global) as the engine of the duality proof and of computations for decompositions.
computation.source: Miller, MIT 18.905 Fall 2016 lecture 37: Poincare duality

confusions.summary: H^n is not Hom(H_n,Z) in general: torsion of H_{n-1} appears in H^n (Ext term); the UCT splitting is not natural.
Cohomology groups do not determine the ring: torus vs wedge; same Betti numbers but different cup-length.
confusions.source: Contessoto, Memoli, Stefanou, Zhou, Persistent cup-length, arXiv:2107.01553, Sec. 3

confusions.summary: Graded commutativity forces 2a^2=0 for odd a, but a^2 need not be zero (RP^2 mod 2); cochain-level cup product is not commutative at all, only up to homotopy, which is the origin of Steenrod squares.
confusions.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.2 Cup Product (pp. 206-229)

confusions.summary: Cup and cap products determine each other on (co)homology only when the UCT maps are isomorphisms (field coefficients or free homology).
confusions.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.3, cap product passage

confusions.summary: Poincare duality hypotheses: needs R-orientation (always available mod 2), compactness for the plain form (otherwise compact supports or Borel-Moore homology), and is natural only for maps preserving fundamental classes.
Nonorientable manifolds: integral duality fails but twisted coefficients restore it, H_k(M;Z)=H_{n-k}(M;Z-tilde).
confusions.source: Hatcher, correction notice for p.335 (Poincare duality with local coefficients, Thm 3H.6)

confusions.summary: Kunneth for cohomology rings needs freeness/finite generation hypotheses, which papers often leave implicit.
confusions.source: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.2 Cup Product (pp. 206-229)

confusions.summary: Signs in duality/linking forms vary by book; authors warn signs should be taken with a grain of salt.
confusions.source: Conway, Friedl, Herrmann, Linking forms revisited, arXiv:1708.03754, Sec. 2

confusions.summary: Satisfying integral Poincare duality does not make a complex a Poincare space (local systems matter).
confusions.source: Klein, Qin, Su, On the various notions of Poincare duality space, arXiv:1901.00145, Sec. 1, 8

cap product, its formula, boundary formula and relation to cup product
homological orientation, R-orientation, orientation double cover, fundamental class

intersection form, signature, unimodularity; cup product as intersection of Poincare duals

Alexander duality and other forms of duality
cup-length and zero-divisor cup-length (LS category, topological complexity)
representability H^n(X;G)=[X,K(G,n)], H^1(X;Z)=[X,S^1], H^2(X;Z)=[X,CP^infinity]
integral vs real/rational cohomology: torsion, lattice of integral classes, p-localisation
explicit cochain-level computation on simplicial/cubical complexes (ordered vertices, branching structure)
cohomology rings of BU(n), BT^n and Chern classes as polynomial generators (statement only; characteristic classes are a separate page)
multiplicative structure in spectral sequences (derivations, E_2 = H*(B) tensor H*(F))
torsion linking form via Bockstein and Poincare duality
twisted/local-coefficient Poincare duality for nonorientable manifolds
sign conventions (coboundary, cup, cap, boundary orientation) and how they propagate
Chern character / H^even(X;Q) and cellular cohomology as input to Atiyah-Hirzebruch (later page needs; from memory)

notes: Distinct neighbouring concepts (suggest separate pages or links rather than full treatment here): cohomology operations / Steenrod squares, Wu formula and Stiefel-Whitney classes (2411.08775 uses w_2 and Wu; 2106.05274 uses cup-i products); Thom isomorphism and Gysin sequence (Miller 18.906 secs 26, 35); characteristic classes (Chern classes of BU(n)); sheaf and Cech cohomology (Cech appears in the duality proof but as a tool); generalized cohomology theories/K-theory; intersection homology (Friedman-McClure); Massey products; persistent cohomology (TDA); group cohomology (2106.09195 uses H*(Sigma_3)); quantum/Floer cohomology (Gong 2111.15442 uses cup-length via intersection products); Poincare duality spaces and surgery (Klein-Qin-Su); torsion linking forms; Lefschetz and Alexander duality could be short sections here.
